_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Cradle of Humankind and Human Origins
910.label: Event
910.description: South Africa's Cradle of Humankind UNESCO site contains some of the world's most significant hominin fossils, placing the region at the centre of human evolution.

910.name: Australopithecus Discoveries
910.label: Event
910.description: Taung Child (Australopithecus africanus) discovered 1924 by Raymond Dart; Mrs Ples (Sterkfontein); Little Foot (Stw 573); fundamental to understanding human evolution.

910.name: Homo naledi Discovery
910.label: Event
910.description: Homo naledi discovered in Rising Star Cave 2013–2015 by Lee Berger's team; over 1,500 specimens; evidence of deliberate body disposal challenges assumptions about cognitive evolution.

910.name: San and Khoikhoi First Peoples
910.label: Event
910.description: San hunter-gatherers and Khoikhoi pastoralists are the indigenous peoples of southern Africa, with the oldest genetic lineages of any living human population.

910.name: San Hunter-Gatherer Civilisation
910.label: Event
910.description: San peoples develop sophisticated knowledge of ecology; Drakensberg rock art traditions; trance healing; |Xam language and mythology recorded by Bleek and Lloyd.

910.name: Khoikhoi Pastoral Society
910.label: Event
910.description: Khoikhoi ('people of people') herders keep fat-tailed sheep and cattle; seasonal transhumance; chiefdoms at the Cape; first contact with Portuguese navigators 1488.

920.name: Bantu Migration and Iron Age States
920.label: Event
920.description: Bantu-speaking peoples migrate into South Africa, establishing farming communities, iron-working centres, and complex states like Mapungubwe.

920.name: Early Bantu Settlement
920.label: Event
920.description: Bantu-speaking farmers settle eastern South Africa; bring iron smelting, pottery, agriculture, and cattle; interact with and gradually displace Khoisan populations.

920.name: Kingdom of Mapungubwe
920.label: Event
920.description: First class-based society in southern Africa; gold-trading state at confluence of Limpopo and Shashe rivers; famous golden rhinoceros; precursor to Great Zimbabwe; UNESCO World Heritage site.

930.name: Dutch East India Company and Cape Colony
930.label: Event
930.description: The VOC establishes a refreshment station at the Cape in 1652; settler colonialism, slavery, and frontier warfare with Khoikhoi and Xhosa reshape the region.

930.name: Jan van Riebeeck and Cape Settlement
930.label: Event
930.description: VOC commander Jan van Riebeeck establishes refreshment station 1652; Khoikhoi dispossession begins; slaves imported from East Africa, Madagascar, and Southeast Asia; Cape Town grows.

930.name: Cape Slave Society
930.label: Event
930.description: Slavery shapes Cape society; enslaved peoples from Indonesia, India, East Africa, and Madagascar; Cape Malay culture; creolisation; slave lodge; emancipation 1834.

930.name: Zulu Kingdom and the Mfecane
930.label: Event
930.description: Shaka kaSenzangakhona transforms the Zulu into a major military power; the resulting Mfecane reshapes the entire subcontinent.

930.name: Shaka and the Rise of the Zulu Kingdom
930.label: Event
930.description: Shaka revolutionises Zulu military organisation: iklwa short stabbing spear, bull-horn formation, age-regiment (amabutho) system; expands Zulu territory dramatically; assassination 1828.

930.name: Mfecane/Difaqane
930.label: Event
930.description: Massive upheaval across southern and eastern Africa triggered by Zulu expansion; displacement of Ndebele, Ngoni, Sotho, and others; new states formed (Lesotho, Gaza, Ndebele).

940.name: Great Trek and Boer Republics
940.label: Event
940.description: Afrikaner Voortrekkers leave the Cape Colony; establish Boer republics (Transvaal, Orange Free State); gold and diamond discoveries trigger imperial rivalry and the Anglo-Boer Wars.

940.name: The Great Trek
940.label: Event
940.description: ~15,000 Boers trek inland to escape British rule; Battle of Blood River (Ncome) against Zulu 1838; founding of Natal, Transvaal, and Orange Free State republics.

940.name: Diamond and Gold Discoveries
940.label: Event
940.description: Diamond discovery at Kimberley 1867; gold on the Witwatersrand 1886; Johannesburg founded; Cecil Rhodes and De Beers; Randlords; massive immigration; African migrant labour system.

940.name: Union of South Africa and Segregation Era
940.label: Event
940.description: Union of South Africa formed 1910; systematic racial legislation (Natives Land Act 1913); ANC founded; segregation deepens before formal apartheid.

940.name: Union of South Africa 1910
940.label: Event
940.description: Union unites Cape, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange River colonies; only whites can sit in parliament; Natives Land Act 1913 restricts Black land ownership to 7% of territory.

940.name: ANC Founded and Early Resistance
940.label: Event
940.description: South African Native National Congress (later ANC) founded 1912 by John Dube, Pixley ka Isaka Seme, and Sol Plaatje; petitions, delegations, and passive resistance; ICU trade unionism; Hertzog's segregation laws.

950.name: Apartheid System
950.label: Event
950.description: The National Party implements apartheid — a comprehensive system of racial segregation and white supremacy — through legislation, forced removals, and bantustans.

950.name: Apartheid Legislation
950.label: Event
950.description: Population Registration Act, Group Areas Act, Bantu Education Act, Immorality Act, pass laws; Hendrik Verwoerd as architect of 'grand apartheid'; bantustan policy.

950.name: Sharpeville Massacre 1960
950.label: Event
950.description: Police kill 69 anti-pass protesters at Sharpeville 21 March 1960; ANC and PAC banned; Mandela and others go underground; Rivonia Trial 1963–1964; Mandela sentenced to life imprisonment.

950.name: Liberation Struggle and International Sanctions
950.label: Event
950.description: ANC armed struggle (Umkhonto we Sizwe); international anti-apartheid movement; sanctions; township revolts; state of emergency; negotiations begin.

950.name: Umkhonto we Sizwe Armed Struggle
950.label: Event
950.description: MK (Spear of the Nation) launched 16 December 1961; sabotage campaign; exile in Zambia, Tanzania, Angola; ANC military and political strategies; Chris Hani leadership.

950.name: International Anti-Apartheid Movement
950.label: Event
950.description: UN arms embargo; cultural and sporting boycotts; disinvestment campaigns; Free Mandela movement; Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act (US 1986); growing isolation.

960.name: Democratic Transition and TRC
960.label: Event
960.description: De Klerk unbans ANC; Mandela released; negotiations; CODESA; 1994 elections; Truth and Reconciliation Commission; Mandela presidency.

960.name: Mandela Released and Negotiations
960.label: Event
960.description: F.W. de Klerk unbans ANC 2 February 1990; Mandela walks free after 27 years; CODESA negotiations; Chris Hani assassination 1993; Inkatha-ANC violence threatens peace.

960.name: 1994 Democratic Elections
960.label: Event
960.description: First fully democratic elections 27 April 1994; ANC wins 62%; Nelson Mandela inaugurated as first Black president; Government of National Unity; Freedom Day.

960.name: Post-Apartheid South Africa
960.label: Event
960.description: Mbeki, Zuma, and Ramaphosa presidencies; HIV/AIDS crisis; state capture; load shedding; persistent inequality; coalition era begins.

960.name: Thabo Mbeki Presidency
960.label: Event
960.description: African Renaissance vision; NEPAD; controversial AIDS denialism delays antiretroviral rollout (estimated 330,000 preventable deaths); Zimbabwe 'quiet diplomacy'; recalled by ANC 2008.

960.name: Zuma Presidency and State Capture
960.label: Event
960.description: Jacob Zuma presidency; Gupta family state capture; Marikana massacre 2012 (34 miners killed); Nkandla scandal; Fees Must Fall student protests; ANC factionalism.
